key_insight: Geospatial embeddings can reveal solar siting suitability, with an RF+MLP ensemble achieving a median ROC-AUC of 0.90 across 13 countries.
engineering_relevance: The global 10 m suitability dataset can help prioritize PV site screening before detailed resource, grid-access, and permitting assessments.
method: Learn suitability patterns from geospatial embeddings of 38,591 existing solar sites and their underlying land.
Combine random forest and multilayer perceptron predictions in a soft-voting ensemble.
Apply standard siting constraints to identify highly suitable land globally.
evidence_signal: Validation against future installations in 13 countries showed ROC-AUC gains of 0.06–0.30 over published MCDA methods; the top-ranked 20% of land contained 84% of estimated generation and 67% of installed capacity.
watch_item: Patterns learned from existing deployments may reflect historical development biases, so suitability rankings should not replace project-specific feasibility checks.
paper_title: Global Solar Siting from Geospatial Embeddings
